author: ReviewReader
derivation: Per-case verdicts derived from RFC 9111 section 4.1 and RFC 9110 sections 5.1/5.2/5.3/5.5/5.6.1 applied to the declared conservative profile in contract.md. Written after reading vary-cases.json (mandated reading order) and before running any candidate; the labels are therefore not blind. Where the spec reading and the declared profile differ, 'profile' and 'spec_note' are recorded separately.
note: verdict is what the declared profile should emit (exit 0 match/mismatch, exit 1 null); spec_note records where a field-specific rule or a recipient MUST would differ.

cases.basis: Vary nominates accept-encoding; one field line each side; values are byte-identical ('gzip' == 'gzip'). Identical values satisfy any field-specific comparison rule.
Field names are case-insensitive (RFC 9110 5.1: 'Field names are case-insensitive'), so Vary: Accept-Encoding nominates accept-encoding and the two sides' names denote one field.
Declared profile forbids value case-folding; 'gzip' and 'GZip' differ in bytes.
cases.spec_note: Accept-Encoding content-coding tokens are matched case-insensitively by that field's own rule (RFC 9110 8.4.1 area), so a field-specific reader could return match; the profile's mismatch is over-conservative but never unsound.

cases.basis: accept-encoding absent from both sides; RFC 9111 4.1 permits reuse when the nominated field is absent from both requests.
Nominated field present in the presented request only.
Nominated field present in the stored request only.
Vary member '*' always fails to match (RFC 9111 4.1).
'*' among the members; the star member dominates an otherwise equal list.

' gzip ' vs 'gzip': a field value does not include leading or trailing whitespace (RFC 9110 5.5: 'A field value does not include leading or trailing whitespace'), so removal is definitional, not a value transformation.
Profile does not reorder list members; 'gzip, br' vs 'br, gzip' differ in bytes.
cases.spec_note: Accept-Encoding semantics are order-insensitive as a set of codings, so a field-specific rule could match; profile mismatch is conservative.

cases.basis: Both nominated fields present and equal.
accept-language differs ('en' vs 'fr').
Two Vary members that differ only in case denote the same field name; the nominated field is compared once and is equal.
Declared adapter refuses an empty Vary value (no field-name member).
cases.spec_note: An empty #field-name list is parseable under RFC 9110 5.6.1.2 ('[ element ] *( OWS "," OWS [ element ] )') and would nominate nothing, i.e. match. Refusal is a declared adapter choice, not a spec rule; it cannot produce an unsound match.

cases.basis: 'accept encoding' is not a token, so it is not a field-name member; the adapter refuses it.
cases.spec_note: Such a Vary value is syntactically invalid; refusing is defensible, and a reader that instead ignored the bad member would still not be required by the text.

cases.basis: Two presented field lines ['gzip','br'] have the combined field value 'gzip, br' (RFC 9110 5.2: repeated field names combine 'concatenated in order, with each field line value separated by a comma'), equal to the stored single line.
cases.spec_note: The ', ' spelling comes from the profile; RFC 9110 5.3 lets a recipient combine 'separated by a comma (",") and optional whitespace (OWS)', so ', '-join is one permitted serialisation.

cases.basis: Combined presented value 'gzip, br' vs stored 'br, gzip'; order is preserved, bytes differ.
cases.spec_note: As in case 10, a field-specific set comparison could match; conservative mismatch.

cases.basis: No internal-whitespace normalisation: 'gzip;q=1' vs 'gzip; q=1'.
cases.spec_note: RFC 9110 12.5.3's weight grammar allows OWS around ';', so the two are the same Accept-Encoding value under that field's rule; profile mismatch is conservative.

cases.basis: Non-string field value (5) is refused by the JSON adapter before comparison.
cases.spec_note: adapter-level type refusal, not an HTTP-semantics question.

cases.basis: Non-string Vary value (5) is refused by the JSON adapter.
